prompt.context_jp: 東京第一銀行本店ビル、昼どきの廊下___行き交う行員のざわめきで満たされていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 東京第一銀行本店ビル、昼どきの廊下___行き交う行員のざわめきで満たされていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks the hallway as the topic being described.

feedback.correct_en: は establishes 'the hallway' as the scene-setting topic the narrator will describe. The sentence then tells us what fills that topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present the hallway as new/identifying information, which doesn't fit a scene-setting opener. を is impossible here (満たされていた is passive/intransitive).

prompt.context_jp: 「伊丹」という名前が飛び込んできた瞬間、二人の箸___同時にほんのわずか止まった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 二人の箸___同時にほんのわずか止まった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking what suddenly stopped.

feedback.correct_en: が marks the chopsticks as the newly-noticed subject of a sudden event the narrator is pointing out. This is classic 'event-report' が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the chopsticks a topic being contrasted or discussed, which doesn't fit a sudden observed event. に doesn't fit syntactically.

contrast_examples.en: The lights suddenly went out (event report, が).

prompt.context_jp: 「大バカ者___あなたのほうです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 大バカ者___あなたのほうです。
prompt.prompt_en: Mai is directly rebuking Itami. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: は sets '大バカ者' as the topic ('As for the real fool...'), with contrastive emphasis landing on あなたのほう. This matches Mai's accusatory framing.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly identify '大バカ者' as new information rather than framing it as the known concept being pinned on the listener.

prompt.context_jp: 「伊丹グループの従業員 約1万人の 給与データ___紛失したんだよ！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 給与データ___紛失したんだよ！
prompt.prompt_en: Shibazaki is breaking shocking news. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: が introduces the payroll data as new, dramatic information the listeners don't yet know about. News-breaking contexts favor が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose the data was already an established topic, undermining the shock-announcement nuance.

contrast_examples.en: Oh no, a fire has broken out! (new info)

contrast_examples.jp: あの火事はもう消えた。

prompt.context_jp: 相馬___普段から派手を好まず、贅沢とも節約ともつかぬ中庸の食事を旨とする男である。
prompt.prompt_jp: 相馬___普段から派手を好まず…中庸の食事を旨とする男である。
prompt.prompt_en: The narrator is characterizing Souma. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: は sets Souma as the topic being described in a general characterization. Trait descriptions almost always use は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would turn the sentence into 'It's Souma who...', an exhaustive identification that doesn't fit a general character sketch.

prompt.context_jp: 品書きの端に走り書きされた「岩ガキ入荷」の墨字に、相馬の目___真っすぐ吸い寄せられた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 相馬の目___真っすぐ吸い寄せられた。
prompt.prompt_en: Describing a sudden visual pull. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: が marks '相馬の目' as the subject of an observed event — his eyes being drawn in. Event-report が in narrative description.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn this into a generic statement about his eyes, losing the vivid moment. を doesn't fit the passive 吸い寄せられた.

prompt.context_jp:
「期待されてますね 伊丹グループの 銀座再開発プロジェクト」
「そりゃそうだ 銀座の街___変わると いわれてるほどの 一大プロジェクトだからな」
prompt.prompt_jp: 銀座の街___変わると いわれてるほどの 一大プロジェクトだからな。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits inside this embedded clause?

feedback.correct_en: Inside the embedded clause 「銀座の街が変わる」, が marks the subject of the change — new information inside a subordinate clause typically takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は rarely appears inside embedded quoting clauses like these; it would wrongly make 銀座の街 the topic of the whole sentence.

contrast_examples.en: I heard it will rain (embedded が).

prompt.context_jp: 議論が沈黙に沈みかけたそのとき、末席の花咲舞___意を決したように手を挙げた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 末席の花咲舞___意を決したように手を挙げた。
prompt.prompt_en: Narrator spotlights Mai doing something unexpected. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: が highlights Mai as the specific person — of all people — who raised her hand at this moment. Introducing an action-doer dramatically takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark Mai as an already-established topic in an ordinary comment, losing the dramatic 'it was Mai who...' flavor.

contrast_examples.jp: そのとき彼が立ち上がった。
contrast_examples.en: At that moment, he (of all people) stood up.

prompt.context_jp: 人事部への異動を告げる笑み___、以前と少しも変わっていない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 人事部への異動を告げる笑み___、以前と少しも変わっていない。
prompt.prompt_en: Describing Itami's unchanged smile. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: は topicalizes 'the smile' and comments on what hasn't changed about it. Comparison-with-the-past comments naturally use は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present the smile as new identifying info rather than a known thing being evaluated.

contrast_examples.en: His face is the same as before (topic-comment).

prompt.context_jp: 相馬___口角だけを持ち上げて挨拶を返し、舞___言葉を選ぶのに苦労した。
prompt.prompt_jp: 相馬___口角だけを持ち上げて挨拶を返し、舞___言葉を選ぶのに苦労した。
prompt.prompt_en: Two subjects acting differently in parallel. Which particle fits both blanks?

feedback.correct_en: Both subjects take contrastive は because the sentence sets up a parallel: 'Souma did X, while Mai did Y'. Pairs like this characteristically use は...は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が...が would turn each into event-reporting with no felt contrast. は...が breaks the parallel structure.

contrast_examples.en: The older brother laughed; the younger brother cried (contrastive は...は).

contrast_examples.jp: 兄が笑って弟が泣いた。
contrast_examples.en: Reports two events but lacks the parallel-contrast feel.

prompt.context_jp: 相馬もまた同じことを考えて___いたが、上に立つ者の判断がそう単純でないことも心得ている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 相馬もまた同じことを考えて___いたが…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle inserts between て and いた to add a contrastive nuance?

feedback.correct_en: 〜てはいた marks a concession/contrast: 'he was thinking it, BUT...'. The は highlights that although the action happened, something counters it.
feedback.incorrect_en: が and も don't fit the 〜ている split pattern used for concessive contrast.

contrast_examples.jp: 分かってはいるが、できない。
contrast_examples.en: I do understand, but I can't do it.

contrast_examples.jp: 分かっているが、できない。
contrast_examples.en: Same meaning but without the sharpened concessive beat.

prompt.context_jp: 花咲舞は抱えた書類の束___胸元でしっかりと押さえ、足早に角を曲がった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 抱えた書類の束___胸元でしっかりと押さえ…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks what she presses against her chest?

feedback.correct_en: を marks '書類の束' as the direct object of 押さえ (hold down/press).
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark it as the subject, which doesn't match a transitive action. に would mark a destination.

contrast_examples.en: Press the book to one's chest.
The book is at one's chest.

prompt.context_jp: 路地の奥、暖簾の下がった老舗の洋食屋___二人は落ち着いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 老舗の洋食屋___二人は落ち着いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the place where they settled?

feedback.correct_en: 落ち着く (to settle in) is a change-of-state verb that pairs with に to mark the destination/landing point.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark the location of an ongoing activity, not the endpoint of settling in.

prompt.context_jp: 木のテーブル___はナポリタンとハヤシライスが並び…
prompt.prompt_jp: 木のテーブル___はナポリタンとハヤシライスが並び…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the surface where plates are lined up (static existence)?

feedback.correct_en: 並ぶ (to be arranged/lined up) describes static existence/placement, which takes に for the location.
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks the venue of an action, not the location where things exist statically.

contrast_examples.en: Books are lined up on the desk (static).

prompt.context_jp: 「支店統括部の代表として 私___選びました」
prompt.prompt_jp: 支店統括部の代表として 私___選びました。
prompt.prompt_en: Shibazaki is explaining his own action. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: が here is exhaustive-identification: 'It was I (not someone else) who chose them.' This answers the implicit challenge about who selected the two.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would merely topicalize '私' and sound evasive, failing to assert responsibility.

contrast_examples.en: I'm the one who decided (taking responsibility).
As for me, I decided (less assertive about identity).

prompt.context_jp: 「とにかく… 紛失したデータを 見つけだすこと___先決だ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 紛失したデータを見つけだすこと___先決だ。
prompt.prompt_en: Shindo asserts the top priority. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: が identifies this specific action as THE priority — exhaustive 'this is what matters first'. 〜が先決だ is a fixed assertive pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would weaken it to 'as for finding the data, it's the priority', losing the exclusive emphasis.

prompt.context_jp: 「はい 坂田さん___決めたんです 僕は 全て 坂田さんの指示で やってるだけです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 坂田さん___決めたんです。
prompt.prompt_en: The subordinate is deflecting responsibility onto Sakata. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: が exhaustively identifies Sakata as the one who decided — 'It was Sakata who decided it (not me)'. Perfect for shifting blame.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would merely topicalize Sakata without the exclusive 'it was him' nuance the speaker needs.

prompt.context_jp: 「この ___の味！ 最高だな」
prompt.prompt_jp: この ___ の味！ 最高だな。
prompt.prompt_en: Souma praises the retro taste. Choose the best word.

feedback.correct_en: 昔ながら carries a warm, nostalgic 'unchanged-from-old-times' nuance perfect for a long-established Western restaurant.
feedback.incorrect_en: 昔っぽい is casual and vague; 古くさい is negative ('outdated/stale'), which would insult the food.

prompt.context_jp: 「イヤなこと思い出させるなよ せっかくのうまいメシが ___ じゃないか」
prompt.prompt_jp: せっかくのうまいメシが ___ じゃないか。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the expression meaning 'ruined/spoiled'.

feedback.correct_en: 台なし means 'ruined/spoiled' — a common idiom for something good being wrecked.
feedback.incorrect_en: 台所 means 'kitchen' and 台本 means 'script'; neither fits the complaint about a ruined meal.

contrast_examples.jp: 雨でピクニックが台なしだ。
contrast_examples.en: The picnic was ruined by rain.

prompt.context_jp: 「うまい店… いいえ ありませんよ もう この辺りは ランチの ___ ですから」
prompt.prompt_jp: この辺りはランチの ___ ですから。
prompt.prompt_en: Mai sarcastically wards Itami off. Choose the best expression.

feedback.correct_en: 不毛地帯 ('barren wasteland') is Mai's sarcastic way of saying there are no good lunch spots — perfect for brushing Itami off.
feedback.incorrect_en: 激戦区 means 'highly competitive area' (lots of good shops); 穴場 means 'hidden gem spot'. Both contradict her message.

contrast_examples.jp: この辺はラーメン激戦区だ。
contrast_examples.en: This area is a ramen battleground (lots of shops).

prompt.context_jp: 「データの発見 事態の収拾を 何よりも優先されるべき急務として ___ くれ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 何よりも優先されるべき急務として ___ くれ。
prompt.prompt_en: Shindo issues a stern directive. Which expression fits?

feedback.correct_en: 肝に銘じる means 'engrave on one's liver/mind' — i.e., take deeply to heart. Standard for solemn directives.
feedback.incorrect_en: 心を込めて means 'with heartfelt care' (used for making/doing things). 気を抜いて means 'relax/let your guard down' — opposite of what Shindo wants.

contrast_examples.jp: この失敗を肝に銘じます。
contrast_examples.en: I will engrave this failure in my mind.

prompt.context_jp: 「事件解決には まず現場を見ないと ___ っていうじゃないですか」
prompt.prompt_jp: 事件解決には まず現場を見ないと ___ っていうじゃないですか。
prompt.prompt_en: Mai quotes a detective-work proverb. Which phrase fits?

feedback.correct_en: 現場百回 ('visit the scene a hundred times') is a classic detective-work saying — Mai is playing cop.
feedback.incorrect_en: 一期一会 means 'once-in-a-lifetime meeting'; 七転八倒 means 'writhing in agony'. Neither fits investigation.

contrast_examples.en: A detective visits the scene a hundred times.

prompt.context_jp: 「___ってものも あるんです」(Mai is saying people can resent you unfairly)
prompt.prompt_jp: ___ ってものも あるんです。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word for 'misplaced/unjustified resentment'.

feedback.correct_en: 逆恨み means resenting someone who actually wasn't at fault — exactly what Mai is suggesting could motivate the crime.
feedback.incorrect_en: 片思い means 'unrequited love'; 仲直り means 'reconciliation'. Neither matches a vengeance motive.

contrast_examples.jp: 逆恨みで嫌がらせをする。
contrast_examples.en: Harass someone out of misplaced resentment.

prompt.context_jp: 「給料日なのに 給料が振り込まれていないという 連絡がありました ___ だと思い 事務センターに行ったところ…」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___ だと思い 事務センターに行ったところ…
prompt.prompt_en: Sakata assumed it was just a routine mistake. Which word fits?

feedback.correct_en: 処理漏れ means 'a processing oversight/missed task' — standard banking jargon for a step that was accidentally skipped.
feedback.incorrect_en: 処理能力 means 'processing capacity'; 処理場 means 'treatment plant/facility'. Neither fits the context.

prompt.context_jp: 盗難という可能性はゼロではなく、むしろ「___」だと言外に匂わせた…
prompt.prompt_jp: むしろ「___」だと言外に匂わせた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the idiom meaning 'not entirely out of the question'.

feedback.correct_en: なきにしもあらず is a formal idiom meaning 'not entirely nonexistent / there's some possibility'.
feedback.incorrect_en: あとの祭り means 'too late'; 焼け石に水 means 'a drop in the bucket'. Neither expresses possibility.

contrast_examples.jp: 可能性はなきにしもあらず。
contrast_examples.en: The possibility can't be ruled out.

prompt.context_jp: Mai suggests to the committee that theft is a possibility.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural in this cautious, formal meeting setting?

choices.text: 紛失ではなく 盗難の可能性も あるんじゃないでしょうか
紛失じゃなくて 盗難の可能性も あるんじゃないですか

feedback.correct_en: The original uses ではなく and でしょうか, giving the appropriately hedged, formal tone for an executive meeting.
feedback.incorrect_en: じゃなくて and んじゃないですか sound too casual/confrontational for addressing the headquarters director.

prompt.context_jp: Sakata describes the mix-up between his two subordinates.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing feels most natural for 'each thought the other had taken it'?

choices.text: お互い 相手が持っていったものと思っていたようです
お互い 相手が持っていったことと思っていたようです

feedback.correct_en: 〜ものと思う is the standard collocation for 'assumed that…'. もの here is the abstract 'thing/fact' nominalizer that pairs with 思う.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜ことと思う exists but is used for formal well-wishes ('I'm sure you are...'). It doesn't fit a mistaken-assumption statement.

contrast_examples.jp: 終わったものと思っていた。
お元気のことと思います。
contrast_examples.en: I trust you are well (formal letter).

prompt.context_jp: Itami complains sarcastically about being transferred after the Shinjuku incident.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural for his snide, grudge-bearing tone?

choices.text: あんたたちに ひどい目に 遭わされちゃったからなぁ
あなた方に ひどい目に 遭わせていただいたので

feedback.correct_en: あんたたち + 〜ちゃった + なぁ carries Itami's blunt, sarcastic, grudge-bearing tone perfectly.
feedback.incorrect_en: あなた方 + humble 〜ていただいた is overly polite/humble, which clashes with his resentful complaint — plus 遭わせていただく would mean HE caused it to them.

contrast_examples.jp: ひどい目に遭わされた。
contrast_examples.en: I was put through a terrible experience (passive, accusatory).

contrast_examples.jp: ご迷惑をかけさせていただきました。

prompt.context_jp: Kozo is explaining why he doesn't give his daughter a discount at the restaurant.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural for 'otherwise it'd set a bad example for the other customers'?

choices.text: ほかのお客さんに 示しがつきませんからね
ほかのお客さんに 見本が立ちませんからね

feedback.correct_en: 示しがつかない is the fixed idiom meaning 'can't set a proper example / can't justify to others'. Standard, native collocation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見本が立つ isn't a real idiom. The learner may know 見本 ('sample/example') but it doesn't combine with 立つ this way.

contrast_examples.jp: これでは示しがつかない。
contrast_examples.en: This won't set a good example.
